final_rationale: The verdict remains suspicious because the Actor did not provide genuinely new admissible evidence; the response is a reinterpretation and narrowing of the same evidence already considered. That narrowing is analytically better than claiming a proven control failure, but it does not cure the main gap. The policy requires admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk for rejection. Here, the cited record shows a questionnaire variance (BPROC-030-D), a note calling for follow-up before approval if unresolved (BPROC-030-E), an informal undocumented quality process (BPROC-030-C), and mixed prior performance (BPROC-030-B). Those facts support concern and further diligence, but the file still does not clearly document why the unresolved issue crossed the threshold from follow-up/escalation into outright rejection. This is the key distinction: a caveated, policy-bounded framing can soften an overbroad claim, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats when the caveat itself is the unresolved compliance predicate.
